A.claim: Only a getter on a buffered target flushes the batch. Other getters read the snapshot plus applied steps, so reads whose value depends on a buffered mutation of another object come back stale.

Two records own the script getter path with different mechanisms and budgets. extendscript@1 uses the figma-mirror with a dirty-group 1-IPC refetch, at 1 us p99. gatebackend uses a per-event cache that is invalidated on write, with a p50-only hot budget.

The app's audio callback waits for a plugin worker inside that callback, and no wait bound or miss fallback is given. A stopped or slow worker stalls the whole app's audio. Per-slot budgets also do not sum to a block for chained slots, and the iOS path (no worker) is not specified.

Peer applies now preempt every holder, but any touch-set conflict aborts the whole event and drops its prefix. A long modal or Long command touching nodes peers edit is aborted repeatedly and starves in a busy session.

PhotoCraft's census still says the plugin prints through the host dialog and classes file.print.printers as Net, which is Excluded -9. The print DEC now grants silent printing to any OS queue chosen by id, but a plugin cannot list the queue ids.
REQ and its new test say the per-plugin installId is free with no declaration. OP-COM-host.installid returns -2 {needs} unless [licensing] install_id is declared.

The write-set check compares the whole copy-on-write diff against scope plus created objects. Host-derived recomputation then rolls back legitimate scoped edits: auto-layout parent resize, instance propagation from an edited main component, group bounds, and sibling index shifts on reorder.

Override allows a guest decision up to 8 ms hard before the built-in runs, yet promises key-to-paint within 1 frame. That cannot be met on 120 Hz displays (8.3 ms frame), and a slow overrider adds 8 ms to every nudge with no demotion.

JavaScript on iOS is now QuickJS compiled to wasm and interpreted by wasmi, an interpreter inside an interpreter. Desktop deadlines for input.filter, raster.filter and audio cannot plausibly hold, so the ladder disables JS hot plugins on iOS.

openURLInDefaultBrowser maps to os.openUrl, which does not exist. The URL permission is ui.open_url, which is gesture-only with a sheet each time. The new via adds bus.publish, but the stmt does not map CSInterface.dispatchEvent or CSEvent.
The census still says the plugin result for the 5 Long commands is job.runCommand. The common record now runs Long commands inside an open txn or txn.modal as one history step.
The silent handle twin opens a project with no dialog and does not say what happens to a dirty current project. saveAs {folder, name} does not say how name is validated against separators or '..'.

B.claim: The 14 first-match rules never mention AgentControl, PluginMgmt on enablement, secret PrefsWrite or Endpoint pref_kind. Under this table those commands fall through to rule 14 and are exposed, while CON-COM-exposure@2 makes them Never(N#) or -9.

FigCraft holders edit the live Session in place, abort Arc-swaps back to the mark, and its DocumentHost has no graft or validate. A preempting peer apply can't be grafted under the prefix, and a later abort restores the pre-peer state, erasing the peer batch.

A peer-preempted holder whose touch set conflicts aborts with -4 and loses its prefix, and touch sets include every id read. A modal or Long plugin that read a page aborts on the first overlapping peer edit and fails all 3 retries at 10 Hz. Figma plugins never abort.

Records disagree on whether a plugin can hand a remote URL to the browser. openURLInDefaultBrowser maps to os.openUrl, and help.* routes go to ui.open_url, but exposure rule 2 and CON-COM-exposure@2 return -9 for any remote Url param under DEC-COM-no-plugin-network.

PhotoCraft's census still says plugin printing goes through the host dialog and that file.print.printers is Net, so listing printers returns -9. The decision lets a plugin print silently to any OS queue chosen by id, but a plugin can't learn any queue ids.

history.list requires history.control:navigate, which is gesture-only and needs document scope, but the EffectCraft route maps edit.history.list to history.read. A history panel that refreshes on history.changed (an automatic event) is refused.

Rule 5 derives history.control:navigate for every purge. That permission is gesture-only and needs document.edit:document. Purging caches loses no data, yet a Batch, droplet or automatic run can't do it, and no record gives a cause.
The test and PERM-COM-identity.user say the per-plugin installId is free and needs no declaration. OP-COM-host.installid returns -2 without a [licensing] table, so the 'no declaration' case fails.

Two records define ExtendScript DOM getters differently. gatebackend reads snapshot plus applied steps with a per-event cache, budgeted at 5 us p50 per IPC call (p50 only, on a hot path). extendscript@1 reads the worker mirror with 0 IPC at <= 1 us p99 and omits gatebackend.

The app's audio callback waits for the plugin worker inside the same callback, but no record bounds that wait or says what audio comes out on a miss. A stopped or slow worker therefore holds the app's device callback and stalls all app audio.

Override has a fixed 8 ms hard decision deadline but promises key-to-paint within 1 frame. On the 120 Hz reference iPad and ProMotion Macs a frame is 8.3 ms, so a timing-out override plus the built-in run plus paint cannot fit. The test checks only 16.6 ms.

All QAS-PC-nocrash and TST-PC-nocrash records were removed with no replacement, while FigCraft keeps 17 crash QAS. PhotoCraft-only faults (handoff hang, page hang, missing plugin on smart-filter open, quit during save, native 8bf crash) aren't in TST-COM-chaos.

A.claim: Only window.craft.post can be Invoked, and 'hidden pages always Automatic'. UXP panel handlers run in the hidden context page's realm, because main-document nodes are adopted into panels. They also call __sync, which has no context rule. Every UXP panel click therefore runs as Automatic.

The round-1 fix is incomplete. sync-endpoint gives the command class no hard timeout, but CON-PC-uxp-page-sync-bridge@1 still says every sync call waits at most BUDGETS[PageSync] and then throws -6 PageSyncTimeout. One endpoint now has two records with different timeout behaviour.

Removing the page cap and the -6 refusal leaves visible and context pages never discarded and never refused. Nothing acts when one plugin's renderer grows past its account, so a leaking context page can grow until the OS kills the app under memory pressure.

This unchanged record still says web windows are 'never docked while D-D is open'. DEC-COM-ui-tiers-t1-t6 was changed to 'Decision 11 sets the web mode', so that decision now points to a no-docking rule, while CAP-COM-t6-docked-modes says CefDocked docks every T6 panel.
Dialogs gain a '10-minute idle cancel' with no cause stated. A user who leaves a filter editor or ScriptUI settings dialog open for a while loses their input. No incumbent auto-cancels modal dialogs.

Transfers are capped at 256 MiB each with no cause stated, and __sync's 'larger results as Handle(Bytes)' may inherit the cap. Figma postMessage and UXP fs.readFileSync have no such limit, so a plugin that moves a 300 MB file or video breaks.

The fork is limited to on_wake and recreate_device 'only'. HDR viewer nodes need EDR, scRGB or Wayland colour-management surfaces, which means changing the eframe/egui-wgpu surface format and layer setup. Those changes are outside the fork's scope, and no other record provides them.

This hot record now stores frames as BC7 at device pixels but gives no budget or thread for encoding. A high-quality CPU BC7 encode of a 2000x2400 frame takes hundreds of ms, and 'on close' runs for every panel at quit. Only restore cost is budgeted.

free is defined as reads of prefs, selection, view, session and job state. This round re-labels OP-FC-widget.state.set, a synced document write, as free, and hook.save.data, ui.set and ui.dialog.open also carry free. The definition and its uses disagree.

Input on the cached frame is held for up to 2 s and replayed to the live page. The cache key has no content state, so a click on a stale cached list row can land on a different control in the live page, for example deleting the wrong layer.

The test expects '40 visible pages get 0 -6 Budget', but the caps table allows 32 windows per app and 8 windows and 16 panels per plugin. No record says which cap a visible T6 page counts against, especially under CefWindow, where panels are palette windows.

The unified event set has no cancel event (capture lost because of a tear-off, Esc or focus loss) and only a single 'key' event, with no down/up or modifier-change events. Plugin drags can get stuck, and tools cannot change the cursor on Alt press or release.

The new probation device assumes the OS will preempt a low-priority queue. Submitted GPU work cannot be cancelled, and on D3D12 the probation device is the same per-adapter ID3D12Device. An unbounded loop therefore stalls the UI or forces an adapter TDR, and a 1 s strike prevents neither.

Probation interop covers textures only. Unpromoted L2/L3 bind plugin buffers, BLAS/TLAS, Bind::Tensor, cache.gpu meshes and PagedTexture page tables. Nothing moves plugin handles between the probation and app devices on promotion or demotion.

On web the DEC adds a second GPUDevice with a copy per tile. FigCraft, PhotoCraft and EffectCraft records still say web uses only the page's WebGPU device. WebGPU has no cross-device sharing, so that copy is a mapAsync readback plus upload, budgeted only at 1080p and only inside a test.

The rewrite dropped Linux memfd sealing from all three shm records. A worker that holds the memfd can ftruncate it, and the host's copy-out read of the mapping then takes SIGBUS. Copying out stops TOCTOU but not SIGBUS.

ShaderRuntimeChecks::checked() and the ban on create_shader_module_trusted and passthrough outside craft-gpu were dropped. L1 and L2 need no permission, so plugin WGSL can do out-of-bounds storage or texture access with nothing enforcing the bounds.

On web, pixels are copied by transfer between the page and the iframe shim on every call, up to 4 ms at 1080p RGBA16F. The transport contract says media is never copied, and no web CallClass budget accounts for this. Five chained effects exceed a 16.6 ms frame.
This record still says new and unbounded digests run in tiled submits after UI present. DEC-COM-probation-on-app-device lists it as affected yet moves all unpromoted work to the probation device.
viewport.pass is still budgeted at a fixed 'GpuSubmit tile worst-case under 4 ms interactive'. The new UiPresentPlugin row caps promoted L4 at Vsync(0.12), which is 2 ms at 60 Hz and 1 ms at 120 Hz.

Two components each claim to be the supervisor. CMP-SEC-ext-worker says it starts every plugin process role, while CMP-COM-ext-broker says it is the supervisor. CMP-SEC-craft-plugin-worker also describes a Wasmtime and Cranelift worker, while CMP-COM-craft-plugin-worker includes V8.
The plugin and Paint rows can take up to 0.87 Vsync of GPU time. The app's own document render, compositor and chrome have no row, which at 240 Hz leaves them about 0.54 ms under full plugin load.
The GPU and audio revocation bounds were dropped. 'GPU stops after the current tile' has no bound, and an uncancellable probation dispatch keeps acting after a grant is revoked.

The AOT cache key lost the engine config and CPU features. A cache restored onto a different CPU, such as after a migration or a Rosetta change, can SIGILL the worker, and the plugin takes a strike it did not cause.

PERM-COM-print and CAP-PC-print-sink now say a plugin may print silently, with the dialog optional, to any OS queue by id including network-backed queues. CON-PC-print-sink, TST-PC-print-sink-tests and TST-SEC-pc-print-dialog require a DialogToken or a preset, and allow local printers only.

One ExtendScript entry has two routes: file.executeFile goes to process.run:<decl>, but File.execute goes to os.open, which refuses executables (CAP-EC-route-os-open, CAP-EC-callsystem-process-run). An AE script that File.execute()s a .bat, .command or .app gets -2 or runs, depending on the record.

The base filter refuses clone3 without naming ENOSYS. glibc 2.34+ pthread_create and 2.35+ posix_spawn try clone3 first and fall back to clone only on ENOSYS. With EPERM, every worker and helper thread creation fails, though the record says threads are allowed.

Every confined start runs the same 9 probes and fails closed on any success. The probes include fork, an AF_UNIX socket, exec /bin/sh and open $HOME/.ssh, which full, bundle-children and native-UI helpers are specified to allow. Those plugins never start.

Linux native-UI helpers get the restricted rules plus the Wayland socket through a supervised AF_UNIX connect. The restricted base filter refuses socket() for every family (only socketpair is allowed), so the helper cannot create the socket, and restricted+ui helpers cannot open windows on Linux.

A .jsx that a restricted helper wrote directly in its data folder gets a provenance entry only on a broker move. If the user drags it into a Scripts or Startup folder in Finder or Explorer, no entry and no OS mark exist, so it runs with user authority.

Navigate covers restore-snapshot and purge, and it is gesture-only. CAP-PC-purge-sheet-rules lets cache purges run without a sheet, giving -11 only for history purges. Script Events, background Batch and timers therefore get -11 on app.purge(caches) and on snapshot restore.

On Chrome, Edge and Firefox, package script runs in a Worker over a DOM mirror, so handlers run async. preventDefault and stopPropagation cannot affect the real keydown, submit, wheel or drag event, and sync layout reads cost an unbudgeted round trip. Figma showUI behaviour is not matched.

craft-pshost can read vendor folders but can write only its private temp folder, with no cfprefsd or HKCU write path. 8bf plug-ins that save presets, settings or licence state therefore fail, and no SandboxDenied escalation is offered for file writes.

Without Landlock (kernel 5.9 to 5.12, such as Debian 11, or Landlock disabled), children=bundle is refused. Windows already starts bundle children through a broker request that re-checks identity, so the refusal has a working alternative and splits behaviour by OS.

When the vendor app is already running, 'the call goes to it'. pshost.launch implies a child process with stdio and an exit status, which a forwarded open does not have. A shim waiting on its child or on an output file has no defined completion, so the call stalls until the deadline.

Without Landlock and bubblewrap, only mutating and open calls trap. stat, statx, newfstatat, faccessat2, readlinkat, getxattr, listxattr and inotify_add_watch on any path still work, so restricted helpers can probe the existence, metadata and activity of files outside their folders.

Two records disagree on where probation runs. EC says unpromoted digests run as tiled submits on EffectCraft's own device after the UI present, with forced loop bounds. DEC-COM-probation-on-app-device says all unpromoted work runs on a separate probation device with its own queue.

Hush's L0 sheet has no document.read, yet its profiling window calls render.request, which needs document.read in a session context. Either the gate is not enforced or Hush cannot run. The sheet-derivation test's verifies list leaves out Hush, Seam, Strata and Beacon.

The hosted builds of Halo (AE and OFX) and Strata (AEIO) no longer record their native.restricted L3 sheets or their third-party notices (native_ui, native_host). Their caps still route through ext-aehost and the OFX bridge, so a derived-sheet check passes an L1 or L0 sheet for native code.

Impure built-ins are routed through a nested render.request with an EffectInsert, but OP-EC-render.request has no EffectInsert field, needs document.read and runs at preview priority. An own-layer Echo-class call would then need a grant and would run at the wrong priority in export.

Recovery re-shares slots and fences to live helpers, but native.helper@2 and the frame transport have no revoke or re-import message, and aehost does not map the event to GPU_DEVICE_SETDOWN/SETUP. A helper holding textures from the lost device can fault or render stale frames.

effect.message works only within one package, but aehost synthesises one contribution per PiPL effect and no record says what a package is for hosted binaries. AEGP_EffectCallGeneric between a vendor's sibling effects (Plexus object/effector-class) may get -3 NotFound.

Folder params hash the whole folder at <=1.5 s/GB and hold frames pending until done. A 4 GB Element 3D model library then leaves the layer blank about 6 s on bind and on reopen, where AE renders at once. The stat-keyed reuse by (size, mtime, inode) was dropped.

Helpers are reaped after 60 s idle. Resuming a scrub after a minute then relaunches the helper and reruns GLOBAL_SETUP with licence checks for Sapphire- or Universe-class binaries. AE keeps these loaded, so the first frame is far slower than in AE, and no relaunch budget exists.

Final renders write lossless EXR durable frames for every plugin-imported footage item and plugin effect output. The budget only names the cost and sets no export-throughput or disk bound. At 4K and 8K, export with plugin importers or effects is slower than in AE.

Checkpoints use 'plugin GPU (2x state)', but Ember declares quota_mb 1024 for 640 MB of live state. It is unspecified whether the 1.28 GB checkpoint allowance sits inside quota_mb and the 2 GiB per-plugin cap or outside them.

The op props no longer refuse stateful or stepped plugin callees, yet TST-COM-fx-apply still expects '-1' for a stateful callee. 'Caller class becomes the weaker' was also dropped from both the op and the plugin test.

The rule 'timestamps only through gpu.timing, own passes, 100 us quantum' was removed, while L3 now exposes queries and timestamps feed the cost model. Nothing then stops a plugin from timing other packages' passes at full resolution.

Taint has file provenance only. A plugin can put expression text or AE keyframe data with expressions on the clipboard, or write a project or template file. When the user pastes or opens it, the result is User, so it skips ext-expr and the read-scope closure check.

Out-of-scope Plugin(id)-tainted values feed the plugin's own effect params as the pre-expression value. This changes what the user renders and exports. The other records say exports and presented frames always carry current values.

The background rebake job commits into the drag's cx.group, but cx.group auto-closes at gesture end. The 10,000-frame bake can land after mouse-up. An Undo issued before the job commits can be overwritten when the stale job commits afterwards.

The modal timer and heartbeat pause while a host-shown script dialog is open. A plugin script can edit, then call dialog show() in a loop, and hold the event transaction indefinitely. The project's edits queue and no Stop is offered.

CEP import and EC-T50 now cite D-D, which is still open-owner. D-D's built state is CefWindow (floating palettes) and says 'only docking parity waits'. Docked Animation Composer-class panels are deferred, and 'every web mode' in EC-T50 tests a mode that is not the built one.

Params are a read-only snapshot prepared before arming. The contract does not say that keyframed or expression-driven params (e.g. Sound Keys output driving a ducker) animate per block in playback. AE's PF_Cmd_AUDIO_RENDER checks out params at time, and playback must equal export bit for bit.

The 'optional sidechain' gives an audio effect another layer's audio, but no read-scope check is stated. Input::Audio and audio.read both require document.read for audio outside the effect's own layer.

Socket connects are refused for every origin. This contradicts the user-script decision, which applies the Access Network preference at sinks. User and agent scripts lose AE Socket with no cause, because the network ban covers plugins only.

Previews and final renders wait for fn() misses with no budget. The fn() instance lives in the plugin's worker, and no fuel or epoch limit is stated. A looping or busy pure function, or a plugin worker busy with a job, stalls export indefinitely.
Removing TST-EC-perf-tainted-rig-drag left the tainted-rig drag path with no budget. A drag may hold the last frame on every sample and still pass EC-T56, while Duik in AE updates live during drags.
The test gates the plugin ducker at 0.125 ms per 128-frame block. The contract says 0.125 ms is the host overhead target and 'never a plugin gate'. The plugin budget is 50% of the block (1.33 ms).

The EffectCraft host table drops openURLInDefaultBrowser, which the common CEP mapping routes to os.openUrl, and via lacks PERM-COM-ui.open_url. VulcanInterface reaches only the package's own pages, with no stated result for cross-extension targets.

The new detail makes picked vendor support folders read-write for presets, preferences and licences, but both sandbox records grant only read on those folders, so every preset, preference or licence write fails.

The 10 s no-poll watchdog does not exclude time spent in a vendor dialog or in scanner I/O, where 8bf modules never call abortProc or progressProc. Every Nik or Topaz dialog left open for more than 10 s, and every slow 8BAM scan, gets Stop and is then killed and struck.

Wasm brush engines now run under an epoch deadline of BUDGETS[PenSample], which is 2 ms per call. Because a trap rolls the stroke back and strikes the engine, any wet-media or 4K-brush engine whose single call exceeds 2 ms is killed, so the incumbent brush engines cannot be matched.

Moving U16 and F32 state to 1 MiB RGBA32F pages under the unchanged 256 MiB quota caps the touched footprint at 16.7 MP. Large strokes on 100 MP 16-bit canvases therefore exceed the quota, and nothing defines what happens when they do.
The PICA list omits the DescriptorRegistry suite, which returns kSPSuiteNotFoundError. Plug-ins that keep their settings and profiles between runs through Register and Get lose them.

A concurrent call now starts another process in the plug-in's host group, but the Windows LPAC decision sets a Job process limit of 1. If the Job is shared per vendor-folder profile, the second process cannot start.
Save never waits, so a file saved while a re-render job is running stores stale durable output with no stale marker. On reopen it shows as current, and Photoshop reads the stale composite.

'Newer version with a compatible contract' and 'older' are undefined for hosted 8bf, which have no contract and often no version in their PiPL. An updated binary with a new sha256 cannot be classed reliably.
CAP-PC-hundred-mp-filter now claims incumbent parity for point filters, but the resident and spilled point benches check only the QAS budget plus 20%, with no incumbent comparison.
The test now lists CAP-PC-vendor-app-handoff among what it verifies, but nothing in its measure covers the handoff, such as the vendor-app tree being killed within 1 s on Cancel.
'Proxy or stale within 1 frame' has no defined source the first time a slow filter is applied, when no stale output exists and a proxy would require running the slow plug-in inline.
'Lab U16 as is' is correct only if the native a and b channels already use Photoshop's 0..32768 range. The data plane states only 'U16 L 0..32768'.

B.claim: The detail now makes picked vendor support folders read-write for presets, preferences and licence files, but both confinement records grant only read on those folders. Offline activation and preset saves therefore fail in the sandbox, or the sandbox is wider than its records say.

This round doubles RGBA32F pages to 1 MiB but keeps the 256 MiB cap. U16 and F32 state now covers about 16.7 MP, and one 4K-brush stroke across a 100 MP U16 canvas (about 41 MP footprint, roughly 625 MiB) goes over it. Nothing says what happens at the cap.

Wasm engines run under an epoch deadline of BUDGETS[PenSample] per call, but that row is a p99 target ('plugin 2 ms p99'). As a hard deadline it traps 1% of legitimate calls. A wet-media tile engine with a 4K brush cannot finish in 2 ms, against the 8-missed-frames tolerance.

This round removes the progress and abort mapping, and the 10 s no-poll Stop rule covers only filters. A hung 8BAM, TWAIN, 8BIF or 8BEM module therefore has no stop or rollback rule. Applying the 10 s rule to them would kill scanner warm-ups and long scans that do not poll.

8BFM always holds document.edit and selection.write, yet the same 8bf also runs as a smart-filter re-render, which is the Render context. No record says which grants or ActionControl Play events are allowed there, so a hosted filter could change the selection or document during render.

8LIZ grants (document.edit:all, document.create, document.lifecycle, app.scripts) leave out selection.write and any file permission. Automation plug-ins that Play select steps, or open and save path descriptors, fail mid-run where Photoshop completes them.

An out-of-grant ActionControl Play has two refusal results: errPlugInHostInsufficient plus permissions.request under 'manifest Authorization', and PsHostError::Denied naming 4CC and permission under principal pshost.<class id>.

'Newer version with a compatible contract' and 'older' are undefined for hosted 8bf, which have no contract level and no reliable PiPL version. A newer incompatible plugin, and a Photoshop-saved filterFX that has no PluginStamp, get no stated behaviour.

Concurrent calls start more processes of the same 8bf, and the vendor support folder is now writable. Two instances can therefore write the same preference or licence files at once, where Photoshop runs one in-process instance.

The hot-path budget covers only an unconverted U16 RGBA 256x256 tile. Writes that convert through craft-cms (CMYK, Lab, Multichannel), F32 tiles of 1 MiB with NaN scrub, and Indexed dither re-mapping have no budget.

CAP-PC-hundred-mp-filter now says point filters run 'at or under the incumbent's time', but the resident and spilled point-filter benches fail only at +20% against the absolute QAS. Neither compares against an incumbent, unlike the apron and nn benches.

The band-form test covers only RGB U16, Lab U16 and CMYK U8/U16. The data path gives no stated or tested form for 32-bit float, Gray, Lab U8, Multichannel, Duotone, Indexed or Bitmap, although the callbacks record claims every mode and depth.

A.claim: A provider whose probe takes over 50 ms is skipped. CAP-PC-pshost-format-modules says an Open waits with progress through the 1.5 s 8BIF cold start and never skips, and FilterFile has no budget. JS and Wasm importers on a cold worker also miss 50 ms and are skipped on first Open.

A document's transaction is released only at its save or close, so a run that leaves a result open (HDR merge) holds it in a modal transaction forever and queues user edits. 'At most 32 savepoints' contradicts the 1,000-state runs in CAP-PC-run-savepoints, with no overflow rule.

The target app runs a BridgeTalk body through its script contract, but no principal is named. A plugin could reach another app's full script engine without that app's grants, and nothing says the body runs as Origin::Plugin(sender) or that the user script engine is excluded.

CSEvent, Vulcan and BridgeTalk ride bus.publish: declared topics only, one-way, 64 KiB CBOR, and suite reach goes only to the same plugin id or a declared provider. CSEvent.data and BridgeTalk bodies are unbounded, onResult needs a reply, and the target app's script engine is neither receiver.
This decision lets a lacks item be tied to a work item, which is a deferral. It contradicts CON-PC-psdesc-coverage@1, which allows only network entries citing DEC-COM-no-plugin-network.

brush.engine@1 lanes are capped at 0-7, so a plugin can draw at most 8 symmetric copies, with no stated cause. Photoshop's own Paint Symmetry offers radial and mandala modes up to 12 segments, which Lazy Nezumi users expect a replacement to match.

After 3 missed frames the copies are dropped for the rest of the stroke while lane 0 continues. The committed stroke is asymmetric, which neither Lazy Nezumi nor Photoshop symmetry ever produces, and the user is not told.

Generator receives imageChanged on every edit, and a plug-in may call getPixmap (one 24 MP pixels.read) on each one. No budget limits event rate, coalescing or reads during painting, so generator-assets can slow strokes on large documents.

Sync calls on the web depend on SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics.wait. The web app has those only when it is cross-origin isolated (COOP/COEP), and neither REQ-PC-web-backend nor this record requires that. Without it, every Node-module *Sync call fails on the web.

Oilworks emits gpu, and CAP-PC-brush-engine-gpu says such engines run L3 programs, which need gpu.direct at risk L1. Its sheet lists only document.edit:selection at L0, so the permission is either missing from the sheet or not enforced.

Sheetkit's via points at FigCraft's CON-FC-format.export@1, which writes a node view, not PhotoCraft's format.export@1, which writes a read-only snapshot through CMP-PC-io-registry. Tonemask's via likewise points at OP-FC-app.batch instead of the PhotoCraft batch op.

This capability was added without a contract, its only test is the unrelated C6 automation-decision property, and API-PS-8bf.selection.picker.automation gives no evidence for an incumbent measurement module.

This round, user.current was made to need identity.user, but three records still say it is free. A compat plugin that reads figma.currentUser cannot tell whether it gets -2 or a value, and the TST would assert the wrong behaviour.

Widget events carry the clicker's cross-app user id without identity.user, so that permission is bypassed. If compat maps figma.currentUser in a handler to user.current, the widget needs identity.user, which the exemption list lacks, and Pulse-style widgets lose the exemption.
Compression dropped notice.files_programs and notice.sync from the Tokenbook sheet. A flagship that runs process.run:git and syncs a watched folder now ships with no third-party or sync disclaimer.

shared_key was removed from node.query, and there is no widget-id criterion. findAllWithCriteria({sharedPluginData}) and findWidgetNodesByWidgetId now fall back to a guest-side tree walk, which cannot match Figma's indexed speed at 100k nodes.

Flagship sheets lost their scopes: Flowline, Lens and Tokenbook now say plain document.edit/read instead of :document, and Cutout lost its PhotoCraft selection.write sheet. Connector follow-ups outside the selection roll back with -3, and Select > Subject gets -2.

photo? was dropped from the collab.peers return, but CAP-FC-perm-collab.read and CON-FC-user-identity still include a photo. figma.activeUsers[].photoUrl therefore cannot be filled, and voter-avatar widgets lose parity.

time.*, key.*, marker.*, color.swatches.list, raster.write, scene.* passes and WebGL2 compute return -8, and compression removed the stated cause and the alternative route. They now read as restrictions with no cause.

The context map says a peer or load cause grants nothing. But the elected runner holds ElectedRunner and commits writes to its plugin-data nodes on peer and load causes, which Flowline needs for runner redraws.

Snapshot retention now reads '64 revisions or 10 s' and no longer says 'whichever is longer'. Under the shorter reading, a plugin that pages changes.since after a truncated payload in a busy session gets -4.
Hot-path budgets lost their machine class ('C17 and D-T reference machine', 'nightly bench hardware', 'CI reference GPU'), so they cannot be checked.

Clearing detail removed the widget render vocabulary and its limits: the element list, Image source kinds with the 4 MiB decoded cap, hoverStyle, tooltip and href. A widget that returns a huge data: image has no recorded bound.

'Any other widget permission removes the exemption' does not say whether ui.web does. Figma widgets that open showUI to edit their own state would then need a collab.write sheet in live sessions, although a confined page reads nothing that could leave.
M4 (week 40) exits on GPU L1/L2 with device-loss recovery in all three apps and on T1-T4 docking with C22 goldens. The app tasks that deliver these are all scheduled at M5.
Three of the four M4 flagships depend on app tasks that land at M5, so none of the three can be green at M4.

Relay sends EffectCraft frames, and large FigCraft vector paths, over bus.publish. bus.publish caps payloads at 64 KiB CBOR, which is far smaller than a frame. The frame leg also has no latency budget.
The test requires the top 10 real incumbent plugins of each kind to install and run, at no more than 1.0x the incumbent's time. No component hosts most of these binary or script formats.

Installed VST3, AU and CLAP plugins run out of process, with a round trip on every audio block. No record gives a budget for added latency, xruns or IPC overhead, although DAWs host these plugins in process.

Every target must run beside its incumbent on every class it names, or on all three classes if it names none. Most incumbents (After Effects, Photoshop, Figma desktop, Lazy Nezumi) do not run on hw-linux, so the M6 exit cannot pass.
CUT gates check only kept behaviour and corpus parity. C17 does not gate until M4, so CUT1 (M2) and CUT2-CUT4 (M3) can delete the old runtimes even if the replacement is slower.

Stream Deck software talks to its plugins only through a loopback WebSocket. devices.companion requires XPC, a pipe or a Unix socket and never an IP socket. No record covers the Stream Deck-side companion plugin that would bridge the two, nor who ships and signs it.
Nothing checks background parallel renders against BG Renderer MAX's speed. Suite render permits may also limit parallel:n to fewer workers than the incumbent runs as aerender processes.
The Deckhand targets name no class, so the class rule makes them hold on hw-linux, which has no Stream Deck. The 120 Hz targets also need 120 Hz displays, which no machine class lists.
Two EffectCraft M6 records are still verified by EC-T47b, which moved to VectorCraft at M8, so neither can close at M6. Nothing tests the licence-file route.

The plan caps PR macOS jobs with 'one account-wide concurrency group'. GitHub Actions concurrency groups are per repository, so 15 repos cannot share one, and pending runs in a group are cancelled, not queued.

B.claim: TST-COM-ws15-incumbent-kinds requires the top 10 incumbent plugins of each kind to install and run. Only craft-audiohost and craft-ofx-bridge exist. Nothing hosts Illustrator .aip, InDesign plug-ins, Lightroom Lua SDK or Substance .sbsar, and FilmCraft lists no VST3/AU or Premiere panels.

Deckhand reaches the Stream Deck through devices.companion over XPC, Unix socket or named pipe. The Elgato Stream Deck SDK (and Loupedeck's) gives plugins only a localhost WebSocket on a port the vendor app passes in, so the specified channel cannot talk to the real vendor app.

EC-T49 accepts JS up to 2x slower than UXP V8 and labels this JS1. The real JS1 (TST-FC-js1-bench) and the M6 parity rule both require at most 1.0x the incumbent, so EffectCraft's JS path is allowed to fall behind its incumbent.

C12 allows unsafe only in listed modules: shm, sandbox, surfaces, gpu interop, pshost/aehost ffi, web cef and engine js. Several planned components need FFI and are not listed, so C12 fails on them or leaves their unsafe code unfuzzed.

C16 requires all workers and helpers to open 0 files, sockets or processes. native.full helpers (kiln-live, video-output helpers under D-G) may open any user file, and native-UI helpers talk to vendor licensing daemons, so either the gate fails or those capabilities are cut.

Running VST3/AU/CLAP out of process adds a cross-process round trip to every audio block, with no latency, per-block overhead or recovery budget. 'Time <=1.0x on hw-mac' is meaningless for real-time audio, and one helper per host group lets one crash silence the whole group.

Targets that name no class must run beside their incumbent on all three machine classes. Most incumbents (After Effects, Photoshop, Figma desktop, Cineware, KeyCastr) do not run on hw-linux, and KeyCastr also does not run on hw-win, so M6 can never close.

INC-AE-render-garden-bg-renderer has no throughput target, only UI p99 and matching hashes. Render permits are max(apps, cores minus app render threads), so parallel:4 can fall to one permit and still pass, slower than BG Renderer MAX's N aerender processes.

The EffectCraft ports (Particular, Twixtor, Element 3D, Neat Video...) and the FigCraft proof plugins have only golden, corpus and acceptance tests, with no performance targets. The M6 wall-clock parity run therefore has nothing to measure for them, and speed against the incumbent is never proven.

C17 performance counters gate PRs only from M4. CUT1 at M2 and the EffectCraft and PhotoCraft runtime swaps at M3 delete the old plugin runtimes, and the CUT gates check only behaviour and corpus parity. The hottest swap therefore lands with no speed gate against the system it replaces.

The REQ says Official builds ship without a notice, except Cue. But Kiln, Keycast and Tonemask UXP carry notice.full_access, and the native-helper flagships (Monolith, Beacon, Halo) need notice.native_ui under D-P. A packager following the REQ omits required disclaimers.

The macOS cap relies on 'one account-wide concurrency group'. GitHub Actions concurrency groups are per repository and keep one pending run, cancelling the rest. Required macOS/CUT checks from PRs queued across 15 repos are cancelled, not queued, which breaks the 30-minute PR budget.

A.claim: CON-SEC-licensing-daemons@1 lists codemeter, sentinel, rlm and flexlm with transport=ip-relay, where the broker relays to 127.0.0.1. CON-COM-manifest.native omits those four and says localhost-IP licensing fails with a named reason. CAP-SEC-macos-daemon-rows says IP-only rows add nothing.

The common guarantee is 1 vsync p99 (8.3 ms at 120 Hz) with frames_over_2x_vsync=0. At least eleven cross-app records hardcode UI p99 <=16.6 ms. On 120 Hz displays that is 2 vsyncs, so those budgets pass while the common guarantee fails.

FigCraft grants plugins 'a disclosed, gated network path' (collab.write, 30 batches/s to peers). DEC-COM-no-plugin-network removes network from the vocabulary, and PERM-SEC-n6's 'Instead' list omits collab sync. Either the owner rule is broken or a host channel is misclassified.

PhotoCraft refuses network by a separate mechanism: build policy refuses Effect::Net for plugin origins before the lock is read. Common refuses in sink::net, keyed on any Via chain with a plugin. PC lists no sink::net component, and DEC-COM-no-plugin-network deletes Network/is_network.

Permission enforcement is reimplemented per app. CMP-PC-sink-* and CMP-EC-sinks do not depend on CMP-COM-craft-command-sinks, and EC confine.rs implements FileAuthority itself. The CON-COM-file-access rules (openat2, no-follow, N3, quarantine) would exist three times and can diverge.

The workstream graph has a cycle, ws2 -> ws7 -> ws6 -> ws2 (also through ws5 and ws8). Milestones are inverted: GPU ws5 (M0) depends on ws2 (M1) and ws3 (M2); ws7 (M1) on ws6 (M2); ws9 and ws10 (M3) on ws8 and ws12 (M5); EC stream-m (M4) on stream-d (M5). The plan cannot be scheduled.

The D-D fix in the ledger missed this record. It still says 'docked web panels ... all on' and 'web = CefWindow' in the same sentence, while DEC-COM-d-d is open-owner. DEC-PC-uxp-page-runtime-cef also assumes docked panels follow their slot.

The prop 'secrets in keychain' contradicts DEC-COM-no-plugin-network, which removes secrets from the vocabulary. FC restates the quotas separately and adds a 64 MiB document cap that the common row lacks.

This record and DEC-EC-ec-fonts-install use fonts.install, which has no permission row; fonts.manage was split into fonts.activate and fonts.system. The record's id and title say step 8, but its choice says gate step 11.
PhotoCraft promises <=5 us IPC p50 for a bridge call in every power state. Common IPC latency is 5 us only on AC power, and 30/100 us p50/p99 under Saver and Critical.

Plugins get 0.72 vsync of OwnerFrame when the user is not 'interacting'. Add UiApply 0.12 and that leaves about 0.16 vsync of UI-thread time for the app. Playback and animation frames are not classified, and the GPU row gives plugins 0.87 vsync.

Never-grantable entries are recorded three times: PERM-SEC-n1..n7, PERM-PC-never-n1/n2/n3/n6, and PERM-EC-never-grantable. TERM-SEC-never-grantable-list says there is one list, and DEC-PC-never-list-pc-adds-none says PC adds none.
